title: Newly synthesized histones: passive or active players in the regulation of epigenetic inheritance?

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Pulled the full open-access text (127 KB after extraction) and the Europe PMC supplementary file list. The supplement is 15 image files only (gkag819fig1-3.gif/.webp, gkag819ufig1-7.jpg, graphical abstract; largest 0.099 MB) with no tables, no spreadsheets, no archives. A regex scan of the whole text for GEO/BioProject/SRA/PRIDE/ArrayExpress accessions, Zenodo/Figshare/Dryad links, GitHub repositories and 'Supplementary Table/Data' mentions returned zero hits. The paper's own Data Availability Statement reads verbatim: 'There is no original data in the manuscript.'
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: All biological content (the claim that nascent chromatin is a 1:1 mix of parental and newly made histones, and the described modification-copying mechanisms) is narrative text citing other groups' published work; none of those underlying measurements are deposited with or linked from this article.

a1_downloadable.note: No dataset exists. Verified in the files: the supplement contains only 15 figure images (all under 0.1 MB), and the Data Availability Statement states there is no original data. Nothing to download, so there is no candidate feature table.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessable, and would fail by construction: any label (for example how much of a histone mark is restored after replication) would have to be assembled from other laboratories' published papers, not read from a column here.

a3_inputs_present.note: No input features of any kind are distributed with the article; the figures are drawings of mechanisms, not measurements.

a4_units_stated.note: No numeric data, therefore no units.

a5_enough_rows.note: Zero data rows, verified from the supplement listing and the full text.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits, but only because there is nothing in it.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No counts are claimed and none exist to compare.

a8_label_provenance.note: No label. Any label would be hand-transcribed from figures in cited papers, i.e. a second-hand reading of someone else's published plots.

integration.partner_dataset: none — the article carries no identifiers (no gene, protein or genomic-coordinate columns) to join on
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: with no data in the article there is nothing for a partner resource to be joined to.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: this is a narrative review of other groups' findings and contains no measurements of its own.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence and chromatin context to predict how fast a histone mark is restored after DNA replication.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would need, for each stretch of the genome, its DNA sequence plus the chromatin state before replication, with an unknown number of examples — this article supplies none of it.
plain_idea.predict: How much of a chemical mark on histones (the proteins DNA wraps around) is rebuilt in the hours after the DNA is copied, as measured by replication-timed sequencing assays such as ChOR-seq or SCAR-seq in other laboratories' papers.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Chromatin biologists studying how cells remember their identity through cell division would learn which genomic regions are intrinsically slow to recover their marks; but the data for it lives in the cited primary papers, not here.

ml_idea: None viable from this article. A real version of the idea (predicting post-replication restoration of histone marks from sequence and pre-replication chromatin state) would have to start from the primary datasets this review cites — for example published ChOR-seq, SCAR-seq or iPOND-sequencing experiments deposited in GEO by the Groth, Almouzni and Tyler groups — and would be an evaluation of those accessions, not of this paper.

effort.compute_note: No compute estimate is meaningful; the only downloadable bytes are 0.33 MB of figure images.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the Data Availability Statement — one line, 'There is no original data in the manuscript' — and list the supplementary files, which are all .gif/.jpg/.webp figures. Took under a minute and killed it.

verdict_reason: Narrative review with no original data: supplement is figure images only and the data availability statement says so explicitly.
